_readme: HUMAN-AUTHORED FILE. CI NEVER WRITES BACK (ADR-0042 D6). The update protocol — what a re-baseline PR must state — lives in baseline.README.md next to this file. Read it before changing a number here.
_what_these_numbers_are: Hosted-runner (ubuntu-latest) means, in NANOSECONDS, with a per-benchmark tolerance band in PERCENT. They are deliberately NOT the workstation figures published in README.md / docs/README-technical.md (AMD Ryzen 9 9900X, 12C/24T), which are 1.97x-2.35x faster; gating against those would red this job permanently (ADR-0042 D4, Option D). Regression protection is this file's job; document-vs-record correspondence is COHERENCE's (D7). The two are separate failures and are detected separately.
_dispatch_1_observer_note: ObserverDispatchBenchmark.Dispatch_1Observer is measured but deliberately NOT baselined, so the comparison reports it as measured-but-not-baselined rather than gating it. Its mean sits at BenchmarkDotNet's resolution floor: on 2026-09-20 it read 0.2145 ns with a StdDev of 1.6012 ns - seven times the mean - and BenchmarkDotNet raised ZeroMeasurement, "the method duration is indistinguishable from the empty method duration". A percentage band around a figure that small tracks the harness, not the code: it produced the two largest breaches in issue #275 (+77.19% and +66.49% FASTER) on runs where nothing in this repository changed. The published ~0.21 ns/observer figure (README.md) is unaffected - it is COHERENCE against Tests/Verbara.Sdk.Benchmarks/performance-record.json (ADR-0042 D7) - and dispatch cost stays gated by Dispatch_10Observers and Dispatch_100Observers. Restore a band only if the benchmark is rewritten to measure a workload above the floor.
_channel_manager_one_subscriber_note: ChannelManagerBenchmark.Update1000ChannelStates_OneSubscriber is baselined on BYTES only (208,000 B per thousand observed changes, exact). It is the same thousand state changes as Update1000ChannelStates on a table with one subscribed handler - the shape of every production host - added because the unsubscribed row cannot see what an observed change costs. Its time has no hosted-runner observations, and a band guessed from a workstation would not match the runner (Update1000ChannelStates reads about 66 us on ubuntu-latest and about 35 us on the workstation), so its mean_ns/tolerance_pct are set from two weekly runs, in their own PR.
_bytes_note: BYTES DECIDE, TIME INFORMS. `bytes` is BenchmarkDotNet's Memory.BytesAllocatedPerOperation and `bytes_tolerance` an absolute two-sided bound in bytes (0 = exact). Allocated bytes do not depend on the CPU, its vector width or the runner fleet, so they are calibrated where they are measured: two local runs on .NET 10.0.14, one with the JIT at x86-64-v3 and one at x86-64-v4, gave identical bytes on every row below, while an interleaved run moved time by at most about 5% on that host; the spread across hosted runners is what a re-calibration under the ISA pin measures. Rows with `bytes` and no `mean_ns` are gated on bytes only until two weekly runs give their time band. The two AsyncEventPumpBenchmark rows carry a 1 KB bound: the per-pump fixed cost of its lock, waiter list and run log, while the 10,000 slots themselves are exact. EnqueueAndConsume1000Events is not baselined on bytes at all: it is bimodal by a writer/consumer race (about 32 KB or about 50 KB), so equality is not a bar for it.
_isa_note: `jit_isa` pins what the comparison expects the JIT to target. ubuntu-latest mixes AMD EPYC 7763 (no AVX-512, x86-64-v3) and EPYC 9V74 (AVX-512, x86-64-v4), and .NET 10 uses AVX-512 where it exists, so the same code read faster or slower by host. The workflow sets DOTNET_EnableAVX512=0 for the whole job (DOTNET_EnableAVX512F=0, the older name, is accepted and ignored by .NET 10.0.14: the JIT still reports x86-64-v4), and the comparator fails closed when a BenchmarkDotNet log names any other ISA. The time bands below were calibrated before the pin, pooled across both CPUs; a re-calibration under the pin is its own PR, from observed runs.

calibration.method: Parsed the BenchmarkDotNet `-report-full-compressed.json` artifacts of 13 real runs of .github/workflows/perf-regression.yml — 12 scheduled (weekly cron) plus 1 workflow_dispatch. `mean_ns` is the mean of those per-run means; the band is set to cover the observed across-run spread with headroom.
calibration.why_the_bands_are_wide: ubuntu-latest alternates between two CPU models and the EPYC 9V74 is uniformly faster — up to 20.7% on some benchmarks. Bands are POOLED across both fleets: one band per benchmark, wide enough for either CPU, because the workflow cannot choose its host. Within-run CV is 0.11%-0.67%; across-run CV is 0.5%-11.2%. This is why a band is NEVER derived from `Statistics.StandardDeviation` in a report — that is the within-run figure and is roughly 20x too tight, and a gate built on it would be red most weeks for reasons that have nothing to do with this repository's code.
calibration.verification: 0 breaches across all 13 runs under these bands; tightest headroom 5.8 percentage points.
calibration.two_sided: Bands are two-sided. The SLOWER side is the regression this gate exists to catch. The FASTER side is a stale-baseline signal (ADR-0042 D6) or a benchmark whose work got optimised away — it is reported as its own kind of breach, not as good news.

sources._comment: artifacts subdirectory (relative to --artifacts-root) -> the BenchmarkDotNet type whose report MUST be there. One row per `--filter` step in .github/workflows/perf-regression.yml. Adding a filter step obliges a row here AND its baseline entries below; a row whose results/ directory or report file is missing is a HARD failure, which is what closes the `|| true` hole (ADR-0042 D4).
sources._turn_detection_note: Present here with NO rows in "benchmarks" below, and that is deliberate rather than an oversight. The step must run and produce a report — a missing results/ directory is still a hard failure, which is the point — but its band cannot be calibrated yet: every other band in this file came from 13 observed runs and this benchmark has none. Its band is set in the PR that flips PERF_GATE_ENFORCE, from its own observations. Guessing one here would break the rule this file exists to enforce, in the change that wrote it.
